academic.passage: The study of neuroplasticity explores how the brain changes in response to learning experiences and injuries. It highlights that the brain is not static but rather dynamic, capable of forming new connections. For instance, when individuals practice a skill repeatedly, such as playing a musical instrument, their brain structure can alter to accommodate this new information. Such findings have significant implications for rehabilitation after brain injuries, suggesting that targeted cognitive exercises can aid recovery. Overall, neuroplasticity emphasizes the importance of lifelong learning and mental activity for maintaining cognitive health.

options: Neuroplasticity enables the brain to adapt and change.

daily.passage: Attention students: The campus library will be closed for maintenance from Monday to Wednesday next week. Please plan accordingly and check online resources during this time.

From Wednesday to Friday next week.
